Tool use:
- read files with read_file, never shell cat/head/tail
- search with search_text, never shell grep/rg
- list with list_dir, never ls
- shell for what the file tools cannot do: commands, git, the network, the system
- batch independent tool calls into one reply — they run in parallel
- end your turn with your findings — never end on a bare tool result
- read_file — whole files or offset/limit ranges, workspace-relative paths
- list_dir — directory entries (the workspace ls)
- search_text — regex search over workspace files
- write_file — create or replace a whole file
- edit_file — replace oldText with newText (never rewrite whole files)
- shell — any command the task needs (builds, tests, git, curl, system queries)
Active tool guidelines:
- read_file: read only the range you need — offset/limit beat whole-file reads
- list_dir: narrow to a subdirectory when the listing caps at 200 entries
- search_text: narrow the pattern when the result caps — never re-run a broad search
- write_file: write/edit: cite the file's latest revision as expectedRevision; each successful mutation returns the next one; use "absent" only to create
- edit_file: write/edit: cite the file's latest revision as expectedRevision; each successful mutation returns the next one; use "absent" only to create
- shell: commands run in the workspace root; on failure read the error and adjust — never repeat blindly
